Field-level EDA: Hibler Farms

A field, field-year and within-grower look at the derived field boundaries, CDL crop history, and gridded weather for one Missouri farm, built from the reusable eda-field subskill's 10 figures and 10 CSV tables.

Grower Hibler Farms (mo-grower) · farm hibler-farms · run generated 2026-11-21 04:54 UTC · this file is committed; the runtime artifacts are not.

  • 40 fields
  • 1185.6 derived acres
  • 2021–2025 CDL
  • 2021–2025 weather
  • 1 grower

1. Dataset scope and grower location

The farm is in west-central Missouri, at roughly 39.03° N, 94.04° W — about 30 miles east of Kansas City. The 40 field centroids span roughly 25 km east–west and 10 km north–south: one local neighbourhood with several separated clusters, not a multi-county operation. All spatial work is done in local metres (UTM zone 15N) to avoid degree-based distance errors.

The data are a single farm snapshot, not a longitudinal farm business record. The boundary layer describes 2026 as-applied coverage; CDL gives the preceding five years of land cover; weather gives the same five seasons. There is no yield, soil-test, machine-log, or management-record layer in this run.

Boundaries are derived, not surveyed: the manifest warns that headlands not covered by as-applied points are excluded and that a few percent area difference from nominal acreage is expected.

3. What each visualization shows

Each category has two statistical views and one comparison view. Numbers behind every panel are in the matching CSV in the runtime artifact folder.

4. What the comparison and correlation analysis shows

  • Rotation consistency. 32 of 38 fields flip crop between the last CDL year and the 2026 planted record; 6 repeat. A two-sided binomial test gives p = 0.0000. With n = 38 comparable fields this is a structural check, not evidence that the grower deliberately rotates.
  • CDL purity vs. field area. Spearman ρ = 0.202 (p = 0.2103) between dominant-class share and log area. The relationship is weak: small and large fields both reach high purity, and the low-purity cases are specific field-years rather than a size effect.
  • Name token vs. measured area. 27 of the 30 fields with a numeric acreage token are within 15 % of it (range 86.8–104.6 %). The exceptions are 21ac-clay-7 (125.6 %), 46ac-m-d (117.4 %), 14ac-lclark (76.3 %). The name is a label; the derived geometry is the measurement.
  • Shape and fragmentation. 19 of 40 boundaries are multipart (21ac-clay-7, 46ac-m-d, 23ac-north-brady, 50ac-bttms, 80ac-don, 71ac-bttms, 25ac-osb, 17ac-iwillis, 35ac-flot, 30ac-weshouse, 10ac-m-d, 14ac-lclark). Multipart fields have lower compactness; 80ac-don is the extreme case at 0.15 compactness with 6 parts.
  • Adjacency. 3 pairs share a boundary (backside-2/richardson-frontside (108.9 m), 25ac-osb/50ac-north-brady (12.7 m), 23ac-north-brady/33ac-south (4.5 m)); the closest pair that does not touch is 23ac-north-brady/40ac-brady-backside at 1.5 m. 21 pairs sit within 50 m and 37 within 250 m, so the farm is several tight clusters rather than one block. The full table spans up to 24.5 km; one pair has a 0.025 ac sliver overlap, a boundary artefact rather than a duplicated field.
  • Weather variance. Season-total GDD varies far more by year than by field: year explains 99.8 % of the variance, field 0.05 %, and the residual 0.20 %. The field term reflects the 2 nearby grid cells, not an agronomic contrast.

Median purity across all 200 field-years is 93.8 %. These 17 cases fall below the 70 % reference line; they are the places where a single dominant-class label hides a mixed or edge-affected footprint.

5. What the geospatial map shows

The portfolio map is the only map in this run. It places all 40 derived boundaries on one local-metre frame with a north arrow, numbers each field, colours by 2026 crop, and gives ID and acres in the key. The overview keeps the true extent; the detail panel expands the largest contiguous cluster so the dense core stays legible. It shows that the farm is a set of separated clusters, that 19 fields are multipart, and that 3 pairs share a boundary. A CDL raster map was not produced because the run ingests the CDL composition table, not the source raster; the map therefore carries crop as a field-level attribute rather than a per-pixel layer.

6. Limitations, missing data, and assumptions

  • One grower only. Across-grower comparison is not identified. The variance partition skips the grower term and says so, instead of presenting a zero as evidence.
  • Few weather series. All 40 fields resolve to 2 gridded weather cells (the tables store field centroids, but fields in the same cell share identical daily values). Field-level weather replication is therefore weak or absent; the field share of GDD variance is 0.05 %.
  • Derived boundaries. Footprints come from buffered as-applied points, not survey or platform exports. Headlands can be missing, and area can differ from nominal acres by a few percent. Shape metrics describe the derived polygon, not the legal field.
  • Names are labels. The “10ac”, “21ac” tokens are not used as measurements. The area-ratio panel only flags where the label and the geometry disagree enough to be worth a look.
  • CDL is coarse land cover. A 30 m raster summarised inside a field boundary mixes edge pixels, strips, and neighbouring land. Low purity is ambiguous between a real mixed year and boundary contamination. CDL is also not a management record and does not prove what was planted.
  • Short panel, small n. 5 CDL years and 200 field-years support description and structural checks, not causal inference. The rotation binomial p-value and the purity correlation are reported as diagnostics; neither is treated as agronomic evidence.
  • Planted-record fallback. 6 of 40 manifest entries had no field_slug. Those fields were resolved by a unique normalized field_name match against the boundary table, and a Planting record outranks a Grain Harvest record for the same field. 40 fields resolved; no field was left as “no planted record”.
  • Not in scope. No yield, irrigation, fertility, pest, economics, or soil-moisture layer. Weather is gridded reanalysis, not an on-farm station.

7. Soil analysis

Soil analysis was not required and was not the focus of this EDA. No soil sampling, texture, nutrient, pH, organic-matter, or plant-available-water analysis was performed, and no conclusion in this report depends on soil properties. The CDL layer is crop and land-cover history; despite living beside soil tooling in the repository, it is not a soil measurement.

8. Reproducing the report

The report is assembled from the runtime folder written by the reusable subskill. Nothing in that folder is committed. To regenerate:

python my-farm-advisor/eda/eda-field/scripts/field_eda.py \
  --data-root ~/my-farm-advisor-runtime \
  --grower-slug mo-grower --farm-slug hibler-farms
python reports/build_field_eda_report.py \
  --data-root ~/my-farm-advisor-runtime \
  --grower-slug mo-grower --farm-slug hibler-farms

The run writes 10 PNG figures, 10 CSV tables, and run_summary.json under derived/analysis/eda-field/. The CSVs are the source of every number in this HTML; the images are inlined here so the committed file opens on its own.
